subject: Python Programming

prompt.value: Let n be some positive integer. word is some string. Both n and word are already defined. The following is a code snippet and the output produced by it. The output produced is 'kindkindkindkindkindkind'. Select all possible values that the string word can take. Note that each option is associated with a different value of n.

# n and word are already defined
out = ''  # there is no space between the quotes
for i in range(n):
    out = out + word
print(out)
# Output:
# kindkindkindkindkindkind

explanation.value: out is word repeated n times = 'kind' * 6. word * n must equal 'kind'*6, so word can be 'kind' (n=6), 'kindkind' (n=3), 'kindkindkind' (n=2) or the whole string (n=1). 'kindkindkindkind' (4 copies) and 5 copies do not divide 6 copies evenly.

prompt.value: M is a matrix (list of lists) that has already been defined. The dimension of M is m x n. Assume that both m and n are greater than or equal to 2. All the elements of M are integers. Select all correct options about the code given above.

# M is a matrix (list of lists) that has already been defined
n = len(M[0])
flag = True
for i in range(n):
    if M[0][i] - M[-1][i] != 1:
        flag = False
print(flag)

options.value: This code will print True if each element in the last row of the matrix is one more than the corresponding element in the first row of the matrix.
This code will print True if each element in the first row of the matrix is one more than the corresponding element in the last row of the matrix.
This code will print True if each element in the last column of the matrix is one more than the corresponding element in the first column of the matrix.
This code will print True if each element in the first column of the matrix is one more than the corresponding element in the last column of the matrix.
This code will throw an error if the matrix is rectangular (m ≠ n).
This code will NOT throw an error if the matrix is rectangular (m ≠ n).

explanation.value: flag stays True only when M[0][i] - M[-1][i] == 1 for every column i, i.e. each first-row element is one more than the last-row element (option 2). n = len(M[0]) iterates over valid column indices, so no error occurs even for rectangular matrices (option 6).

prompt.value: The following code always accepts a positive even integer as input. What is the output produced by the code if the input is 199999978? Hint: 99999989 is a prime number.

n = int(input())
f = n - 2
while (f > 0) and (n % f != 0):
    f = f - 2
print(f)

explanation.value: f steps down by 2 from n-2 until it divides n. 199999978 = 2 * 99999989, and 99999989 is prime, so the only even divisors are 2 and 199999978; the largest even proper divisor found is 2.
